join_order.notes: Use movie_keyword__keyword_id CSR; target_k_id resolved by scanning keyword.dat. Very small mk row set.
cn_pass bitmap indexed by cn.id (size 234997). '[nl]' is rare → low popcount. For each candidate movie from mk, scan mc rows via movie_companies__movie_id offsets and test cn_pass[company_id].
title.id is dense identity; mv is the row index directly. Read t.title via title.off/title.dat for surviving movies.

data_structures.cn_pass: bitset(234997) — flat bool/uint8 array indexed by cn.id

parallelism.notes: Driver set (mk rows for one keyword) is very small; thread overhead exceeds work. Run serial.

execution_recipe: 1. Memory-map all required column files and index files.
3. Build cn_pass: bitset of size 234997; for r in [0, 234997): cn_pass[r] = (country_code_bin[r] == target_code).
4. Scan keyword/keyword.off+dat to find row whose string == 'character-name-in-title'; target_k_id = keyword.id[row].
5. Using movie_keyword__keyword_id CSR: lo=off[target_k_id], hi=off[target_k_id+1]. For each k_pos in [lo,hi): mk_row=rowids[k_pos]; mv=mk.movie_id_bin[mk_row].
6. For each candidate mv: using movie_companies__movie_id offsets, iterate mc rows r in [off[mv], off[mv+1]); if cn_pass[mc.company_id_bin[r]] true → mv qualifies; break inner.
7. For qualifying mv: read title.title via title.off[mv]/title.off[mv+1] into string_view; update min_title (lexicographic).
